title: Potato Anatomy, Metabolism & Ecology — Cell to Tuber to Soil
purpose: Map the physical potato from organelles and cells through tissues and organs to resource flows and microbial/ecological niches.

outer_boundary.epidermis: Present transiently in very young tubers.
outer_boundary.periderm: Replaces the epidermis and contains phellem, phellogen and phelloderm.
outer_boundary.suberin: Hydrophobic barrier polymer important for limiting water loss and pathogen penetration.
outer_boundary.lenticels: Specialized gas-exchange structures through the periderm; their state varies with development, moisture and storage.

flesh.cortex_and_parenchyma: Living storage tissue occupying much of the tuber; cells contain abundant amyloplasts.
flesh.vascular_ring: Connects the tuber to phloem/xylem transport and organizes imported resources.
flesh.pith_medulla: Inner tissue region continuous with stem developmental organization.
flesh.eyes: Node/bud complexes distributed over the stem-derived tuber surface.

carbon_cycle: leaf chloroplast: photons + CO2 → fixed carbon
mitochondria: respiration supplies ATP and metabolic intermediates

mineral_water.roots: take up water and mineral nutrients
mineral_water.xylem: moves water/minerals upward through transpiration-driven and pressure-related processes
mineral_water.phloem: redistributes carbon, nutrients and signals among sources and sinks
mineral_water.potassium: major nutrient strongly associated with potato yield, osmotic regulation and tuber quality; optimum supply is context dependent
mineral_water.nitrogen: supports canopy/protein synthesis but excessive or poorly timed N can delay maturity and alter tuberization/quality
mineral_water.calcium: important for membranes/cell walls and tuber quality; delivery to tubers is constrained by transport physiology
mineral_water.phosphorus_magnesium_sulfur_micronutrien: contribute to energy metabolism, photosynthesis, enzymes and quality traits

secondary_metabolism.steroidal_glycoalkaloids: alpha-solanine and alpha-chaconine are defense-related metabolites; biosynthesis involves cholesterol-derived pathways including GAME-family enzymes.
secondary_metabolism.pigments: anthocyanins and carotenoids contribute cultivar-dependent skin/flesh coloration and antioxidant chemistry.
secondary_metabolism.phenolics: participate in defense, wound responses and nutritional chemistry.

boundary_and_repair.periderm_rule: A living boundary is not sealed completely; it balances protection, water relations and gas exchange.
wound_healing: closing-layer formation: existing surface-adjacent cells become suberized
wound-periderm formation: meristematic phellogen activity produces new protective tissue
boundary_and_repair.lenticel_tradeoff: Lenticels enable O2/CO2 exchange but can also provide pathogen entry opportunities; wet/low-oxygen conditions can alter lenticel morphology.

microbiome.caution: Microbiome composition is dynamic and environmentally acquired; 'potato microbiome' is not one fixed species list.

environmental_biophysics.gas_exchange: Leaves use stomata; tuber gas exchange relies heavily on lenticels/periderm permeability.
environmental_biophysics.water: Water availability influences canopy growth, cell expansion, tuber set and bulking; both drought and waterlogging create stress.
environmental_biophysics.temperature: Heat can inhibit tuberization and accelerate stress/senescence; cold storage reshapes tuber metabolism.
environmental_biophysics.mechanics: Cell-wall expansion, turgor and tissue mechanics contribute to tuber swelling and organ shape.
environmental_biophysics.light: Leaves require light for photosynthesis; direct tuber exposure causes greening and is associated with quality/defense-metabolite changes.
